transcript: I had a lot of people wondering what happens to the Broadway theater after Here Lies Love closes. Right now, they are in the middle of pulling out all of the seats in the orchestra to essentially turn it into this where you have the mezzanine and then an entire dance floor. So the show is going to be performed essentially in the orchestra. So what happens when the show closes? Short answer is they just put it back. They put it back to the way that it was. Seats and theaters were made to be removed easily, and they kind of do this more often than you would think. Most likely, it's just the first few rows to put in an orchestra pit. If you've ever been in a theater and it doesn't start with row A, that's because rows have been removed or added. Sometimes you'll see an A, A, A, B, B, C, C, or maybe it'll start at row C for some reason. That's because those. Those rows were taken out. But there is. There have been shows on Broadway that have renovated a theater as much as Here Lies Love is doing. Most recently, of course, one of my favorite scenic designs ever, Great Comet. This fantastic set design, which was done by scenic designer Mimi Leon, is fantastic. And they also put the stage essentially in the middle of the orchestra. This photo is taking from seats that were placed onto what is normally The stage, and then you can see the mezzanine and the orchestra seats, for the most part, remained intact. But if you look at the theater when it's empty, you can see that there's a walkway going down the center of the orchestra seats. Also, if you look at, like, the little lights coming from the orchestra and the mezzanine, those were lamps placed on tables. And that all of the tables were where a seat once was. So you can, in fact, remove just a single seat, and then the rest of the row is still there. This is a different view from the mezzanine of the theater, where you can see the proscenium of the Imperial Theater. And then once the show closed, just like they do with any show, they struck the set. And in this case, that meant taking out all of this set that they had built out and putting all the chairs back in. So now when you go into the Imperial, it just looks like this, like a normal theater. But, yeah, it's kind of cool what you can do with scenic design.
